_note: Our own writing. The part of space the squad works in: a few systems joined by blink gates, which the book describes as common, fast and safe (Core p.10), each with a few worlds, moons or stations. Every world has its own culture kit and landscape (cultures.json) and one hub. Travel is narrative: no costs or travel time are tracked (CANON.md parks paid travel). Interstellar travel without a gate happens at near light speed, so time passes differently for travellers (Core p.20); the game only travels by gate between systems.

local: {patron_ship} carries the squad from {from} to {to}. A few days in transit, mechs strapped down in the hold.
The squad hitches a ride on an ore hauler from {from} to {to}. Nobody asks what's in the crates, on either side.
A short hop across the system, from {from} to {to}. Long enough to sleep, check the mechs, and argue about the next job.
gate: Out of {from}, through the blink gate, and out again in the {system} system. It takes no time at all, and it never stops feeling strange.
The ship lines up on the blink gate and slips through. On the other side is the {system} system, and {to}.
A queue at the gate, a moment of nothing, and then a new sky: the {system} system. {to} is a short flight in.
